clue.text: Has pulling power — deploying odd legs, for example

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: the animal is one that has pulling power

indicators.note: deploying means arranging or spreading out, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Something with towing strength is illustrated by a creature putting its odd legs to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deploying' rearranges ODD LEGS plus EG. The definition is loose: it describes the animal by what it does rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Teams of these huskies are harnessed to haul sleds across snow, so traction is their job.

clue.text: A pound the military accepted for getting measure of land

indicators.note: accepted means took in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for stray animals, a cage
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a pound sterling to the army in exchange for land being surveyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money but is an animal enclosure; the Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Area expressed in acres is the extent of a plot of land.

clue.text: Can't drop off? Funny — Simon and I can!

definitions.note: describes a person who cannot fall asleep, standing for the noun

indicators.note: funny here means peculiar or odd, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A joke that two people, Simon and the speaker, are both unable to get to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges SIMON, I and CAN; 'and' is only a link. The definition describes the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering chronic sleeplessness lies awake, unable to nod off.

clue.text: Quip in kindly fashion? With sarcasm!

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark, such as a pun
gently means in a kindly, mild manner

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a witticism was meant kindly and is told it was sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting, sharp-tongued remark is delivered cuttingly, with stinging sarcasm.

clue.text: Hawk, non-flier

parts.note: hawk taken not as the bird of prey but in its other sense, to sell goods by going about offering them

explanation.surface: A bird of prey that cannot fly.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk wares is to go round selling them, as a street vendor does.

clue.text: Corruption results when the Frenchman joins the mob

parts.note: a mob is a gang
Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Moral decay sets in once a Frenchman falls in with a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' is only a link; René is a stock French name in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangrene is the rotting decay of body tissue, a physical corruption.

clue.text: Identification of magenta weave

indicators.note: weave means interlace, so the letters are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A badge for identifying someone is woven in a magenta colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge bearing a person's name serves to identify the wearer.

clue.text: A few words omitted when sporting play resumes?

definitions.meaning: a line of text left out or crossed out of a script
in rugby, the set piece restarting play after the ball goes into touch

explanation.definitionFit: A cut line of dialogue is struck out; in rugby union the restart throw-in after touch has this name.

clue.text: What a driver needs the green light

definitions.meaning: the document a motorist must hold to drive legally

explanation.definitionFit: A motorist must hold a driving permit; more generally the word means official permission to proceed.

clue.text: One Scottish warning rejected inside this plant

indicators.note: inside puts the turned warning within the Scots word for one

parts.note: ane is the Scots form of one

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for warning is read backwards

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: A Scot's warning is ignored, with the danger lying within this very plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reads the warning backwards before it goes 'inside' the Scots word; 'this plant' makes the clue point at its own answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The windflower is a buttercup-family flowering plant with bright cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Brazil, for instance, source of pigment

definitions.text: Brazil, for instance, source of pigment

parts.words: Brazil, for instance, source of pigment
parts.note: Brazil read not as the country but as brazilwood, a tree whose timber yields a red colouring

explanation.surface: The South American country is offered as an example of where colouring comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazilwood and logwood are timbers from which colouring matter for fabrics is extracted.

clue.text: Barking at rodent big cat caught

indicators.note: caught means trapped, so the big cat holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Barking breaks out at a rat that a big cat has seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' here is the noun, the act of a dog barking, not the London district or 'mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare Latin-derived word for the yapping noise a dog makes.

clue.text: Straits in which such creative types may find themselves

indicators.note: the creative types find themselves in the letters of the word straits, hidden as a jumble of them

explanation.surface: Painters and the like often end up in financial difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straits' doubles as the hard times artists are said to fall on; its letters rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters and sculptors are the classic creative people.

clue.text: Effect this professional man produced

definitions.meaning: to effect is to bring about or contrive
a qualified technical professional who designs machines or structures

explanation.definitionFit: To bring about a plan cleverly is to contrive it; the noun is a qualified designer of machines or bridges.

clue.text: One wicket? Nonetheless, disallow!

indicators.note: read as none the less: none is nothing, the letter O, and less says it is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
a wicket is a small gate

explanation.surface: A cricketer has lost one wicket but insists the dismissal be ruled out anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonetheless' splits as 'none the less': nothing, the letter O, is taken away. A wicket gate is a small gate set into a larger one.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow something is to cancel or nullify it.

clue.text: Former leading etcher Whistler displaced

indicators.note: leading picks out the front letter of the word etcher
displaced means moved out of position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A once-celebrated etcher, Whistler, has been knocked off his pedestal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' takes the front of 'etcher' and 'displaced' rearranges WHISTLER. James Whistler was an American painter and etcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that once was but is no longer is of a bygone, previous time.

clue.text: Dropping round, doctor lent video to youth-leader? Without question!

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
dropping means leaving out, so the ring shape is removed from the word video

parts.note: round is the ring-shaped letter O

indicators.note: leader picks out the front letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: Someone dropping by has a doctor lending a video to a youth leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping round' leaves VIDE, which 'doctor' rearranges with the other fodder; 'youth-leader' gives the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plainly or obviously true is beyond doubt.

clue.text: Snapper taken from a river by expert

parts.note: a snapper is something that snaps or bites, a biter

explanation.surface: An expert catches a snapping fish from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapper' looks like the fish but is one that bites.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or authority whose opinion settles matters is a recognised expert.

clue.text: Breakwater, to hold it back?

parts.note: breakwater read as break plus water, a pause or rest plus rain, while the whole describes holding something in check

explanation.surface: A sea wall is built to keep the waves at bay.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or keep something in check is to hold it back.

clue.text: Look briefly and fly off

definitions.meaning: to strike something obliquely and bounce away, as a ball does off a bat

explanation.definitionFit: A quick peek is a brief look; a ball or blow that strikes at an angle and deflects is said to ricochet this way.

clue.text: Not a sure-footed dog?

definitions.meaning: one who staggers or sways when walking
a crossbred hunting dog, usually part greyhound

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who staggers about lurches; the noun is also a crossbreed hound used by poachers.

clue.text: Drifting off, mid-ocean, no longer bearing east

indicators.note: off means wrong or bad, signalling a rearrangement of the letters
no longer bearing means the word mid-ocean drops something it carried

explanation.surface: A boat is drifting in the middle of the ocean, no longer heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer bearing east' removes E from MIDOCEAN, and 'off' rearranges the remaining MIDOCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering peoples who move from place to place rather than settling are roaming.

clue.text: Sense new growth, making use of this faculty?

definitions.note: describes the organ by its use, standing for the noun

parts.note: taste is one of the five senses
a bud is a new growth on a plant

explanation.surface: A gardener senses fresh shoots appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the organ is what uses the faculty of taste.
explanation.definitionFit: These sensory organs on the tongue detect flavour, so we rely on them to savour food.

clue.text: Arrive at a race in a flurry

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle race

indicators.note: in a flurry means agitated and confused, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone turns up at a race in a state of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a flurry' rearranges the two words just before it. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a goal or point is to achieve it.

clue.text: Mad artist battered playwright

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazed painter has been beaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of plays for the stage is a dramatist.

clue.text: Gorge, with cheese

definitions.meaning: a limestone gorge in Somerset, England
a hard English cheese named after the village there

explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset ravine and the famous hard cheese from the village at its foot share the name.

clue.text: Rancour shown by ailing swan of Avon?

parts.note: ailing means ill
the Swan of Avon is William Shakespeare, so Will

explanation.surface: A sickly swan on the river Avon shows bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan of Avon' looks like a bird but is Shakespeare's nickname, from Stratford-upon-Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is lasting hostility or malice toward someone.

clue.text: Severe rain can do damage

indicators.note: damage here signals the letters being broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Heavy rain is capable of causing destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws named after the harsh Athenian lawgiver Draco are extremely harsh.
